groups.checked_argument: Gauduchon Stokes holds also for distributional potentials; testing one metric bounds the infimum. Smooth ddc invariance, monotonicity, homogeneous concavity and upper semicontinuity follow from the individual linear quotient.

The matrix arithmetic-geometric mean gives the lower bound. A conformal Gauduchon representative of the solution achieves it. Equality fixes the conformal class, with uniqueness up to scale for n>=2; n=1 is treated by integration.

Bigness dominates delta times a positive Hermitian class. For equality at an interior positive segment, one minimizing metric minimizes both endpoints; fixed volume forms make the endpoint solution forms differ by a constant scale. The curve case uses the Green operator.

Finite-dimensional smooth dependence uses the internal positive-background implicit-function theorem. Multiplication by the Gauduchon conformal factor removes the ddc potential derivative and gives the exact quotient denominator.

Twice differentiating the logarithmic determinant gives constant trace n lambda-prime/lambda. The fixed adjoint probability removes the second potential derivative. Squared trace-free and full Hermitian norms give the two kernels and a positive class metric on finite-dimensional families.

The positive (n-1)st root of the derivative form is normalized by D_mu=1. Its conformal rescaling to the prescribed volume reconstructs the solution form. Every Gauduchon ray arises from its unit-volume conformal background.

Euler differentiation gives a unit radial vector orthogonal to the unit-volume hypersurface. Scaling gives the logarithmic product metric and intrinsic distance formula. Product surfaces are complete; the blowup cone a>b>0 has Euclidean coordinates (r,s), s>0, and a positive-volume nef boundary at finite distance.

Compactness makes invariant holomorphic fields divergence-free by integrating their action on the top form. Closed contractions span invariant (n-1,0) forms, giving balancedness. Zero averaged ddc coefficients characterize positive and semipositive coefficient matrices even for distributional potentials, and exclude nonzero exact invariant directions.

The invariant positive background attains the determinant quotient. A conformal Gauduchon minimizer of a balanced metric has constant factor by the energy identity. The resulting Hessian is the positive matrix trace metric. For nonabelian groups every positive invariant background remains nonclosed after smooth gauges.

Congruence invariance reduces the distance to I. The resolvent derivative of log has coefficients bounded by the inverse geometric mean of eigenvalues, giving the lower distance bound. The exponential path attains it in the full matrix space and in a fixed-determinant hypersurface; it need not remain in a proper W.

The normalized straight segment remains inside W and gives an intrinsic upper bound. Logarithmic distance bounds imply matrix order bounds, compact balls, and convergence to positive coefficient limits. Nonzero singular limits have distance at least |log det|/(n sqrt(n))+bounded error after normalization; zero coefficient limits may normalize to an interior point.

The Gaussian Heisenberg lattice has the written measurable fundamental cube, coframe and volume H=6/pi^3. Averaging a hypothetical closed positive form contradicts its positive A33 coefficient. The diagonal degeneration has exact distance sqrt(2)|log epsilon|/3.

groups.scope: threefold upper mass and zero boundary mass
groups.checked_argument: The invariant complex Hessian is a positive sum of (2,0) squares in dimension three, and balancedness allows the internal threefold maximum mass identity. Semipositive singular coefficients have zero bounded top product by positive perturbations and polynomial continuity, then zero unbounded nonpluripolar product by truncation.

A positive block Schur complement gives a closed base torus equation. Its lifted solution is positive and balanced and has determinant det(A)*f. The vertical Dirichlet defect has exact factor A33 H/2; zero defect makes the smooth solution constant on connected elliptic fibers, characterizing all maximizing densities.

For a fixed fiber-invariant density the coefficient determinant metric is unchanged, with the same intrinsic completion. Minimizer estimates concern coefficient means; no invariant pointwise estimate is asserted for nonconstant minimizers. Constructed fiber-varying densities have strictly smaller volume, without determining completion for a fixed such density.

Closed-base smooth equations give Omega^n=n b^m mu/H. Multiplying Omega by L^(-1/m) makes its cofactor closed and computes the exact minimizing quotient. On the unit-volume slice e=Q(v)/(n b^m), the Hessian splits as m d(log b)^2 plus 2/n times the reciprocal-coefficient variance.

Finite disjoint smooth extreme strata with power-comparable vanishing give the tube integrals H,J,K. Separated annuli prove variance lower bounds for r<1 and the logarithmic r=1 case, rather than subtracting merely comparable moment asymptotics. For r>1 the K bound makes the square-root variance integrable.

The flat product metric gives exactly a strip, half-plane or plane. Finite coefficient limits have unit variational volume by monotone quotients and fixed-test continuity. Testing against arbitrary nonnegative top-degree base forms excludes positive current domination because the fiber coefficient vanishes.

The projective moment-simplex density is 4s and 4(1-s), giving H=4 log 2, the exact Q integral and r=2 finite ends. The torus has real hypersurface extrema of order two, r=1/2, explicit periodic potentials, Q=(1+v)^(-1/2) and a complete Euclidean unit slice.

Positive current tests characterize b>=0 and nonnegative fiber coefficient; nefness has the same cone and strict inequalities characterize bigness. At a finite end, 1/L is in some Lp, p>1, so a continuous closed-base solution pulls back to the endpoint equation. C11 ellipticity would force a positive current domination, which is excluded.

Dominated Lp convergence of normalized base densities plus the internal fixed-background compactness and closed uniqueness give uniform convergence of all base potentials. Local psh corrections prove all mixed-product weak limits. The uniqueness claim is limited to pulled-back bounded solutions, with the full closed-base mass ruling out extra measure on the extreme set.

The cofactor has exact first term sigma/(n L^2) and a bounded-mass closed mixed term. Its trace diverges with epsilon^(r-2) or log for 1<r<=2 and has a finite positive closed limit for r>2. Trace-normalized cluster measures are supported on the minimal-ratio extreme strata; a single point gives the whole fiber current. The two quotient terms decay together and their ratio stays one.

The determinant is taken relative to the trace measure, including any singular trace part. Homogeneous determinant minimization uses Q_epsilon, and Lusin approximation with uniform spectral bounds makes it an infimum over continuous fixed-volume forms. This proves upper semicontinuity and concavity for positive currents without asserting smooth approximation of currents.

Compact normalized ddC-closed currents give a positive attained maximum. The smooth solution form is an admissible fixed-volume test. Equality forces a scalar measure times its conformal Gauduchon cofactor; elliptic regularity and the one-dimensional adjoint kernel make the measure smooth and constant. For continuous F only the data F are approximated, using the uniform multiplicative bounds and normalization Lipschitz continuity.

Perturbing the density by n log(1 plus or minus epsilon h) and using equal total mass upgrades upper semicontinuity to weak measure convergence for near-maximizers. Measure concavity and equal maximal mass give affineness on maximizers.

Jensen gives each maximizing determinant probability as a support. A uniform exponential Taylor remainder and compactness of moving maximizers compute the right derivative as minus the maximal h integral. Separation of the compact convex image gives all supporting probabilities. Absolute continuity uses the previously proved internal adjoint-probability theorem, not absolute continuity of the currents themselves.

Smooth equations with density h^n and the internal Lp lower-density estimate give a uniform dual L(np) test bound. Functional duality yields absolute continuity and Lq bounds for all q<n/(n-1), also forcing determinant zero on the singular trace part.

Positive lower mass gives the dual Ln bound. Smooth probability equations and their normalized Gauduchon factors give equality in the reverse supremum as equation constants approach the lower mass, including an infinite supremum at zero lower mass. The critical constant is independent of the reference probability volume.

Bounded continuous F multiply determinant densities by a bounded factor and have a positive uniformly bounded-below normalization M(F), giving support-density Lq bounds. Positive lower mass gives the endpoint even with infinite upper mass; the explicit Hopf threefold example attains 6^(-1/3).

The two normalized elliptic inverses control a contraction for the log-determinant equation and a contraction for its Gauduchon factor. The chosen radius gives form and factor comparisons using only C(2,alpha) data. Trace normalization by Z and the stated comparisons give exactly C_nu=3^(n+1)a Hmax/4 and C_k=3^n a Hmax^((n-1)/n)/2. The probability normalization gives the sharper critical norm C_nu^(1/n), independent of lower mass.

Normalization of exp(F) is injective on zero-mean finite-dimensional smooth families. The explicit potential path has distinct data by the maximum principle and distinct maximizing currents by a nonscalar Hessian at one point and positive cofactor uniqueness. The constants do not extend to arbitrary near-maximizers.

Smooth positive root densities give the supremum; the subcritical dual estimate gives uniform convergence for bounded measurable approximants. General Ln roots use two suprema and monotone truncation, with no attainment assertion. Vanishing root-norm tails give a finite upper-semicontinuous functional and uniformly integrable weighted determinant densities.

Uniform integrability is equivalent to vanishing root tails by the full supremum formula. Bounded multiplicative perturbations converging in measure then converge in root norm. When tails fail, smooth cutoffs of regular compact tail sets and a fixed exponential boost give an L1-convergent density sequence with a fixed threshold gap.

Uniform integrability along one weakly convergent maximizing sequence is sufficient. Upper semicontinuity for bounded truncated weights gives the limit determinant measure domination; equal total masses identify the measure and the maximizing current.

The tail condition is preserved by bounded multiplicative weights. Logarithmic convexity of the supremum gives a concave threshold normalization. Compactness and affinity of maximizing weighted measures, the uniform exponential Taylor expansion and separation yield all supporting probabilities and both one-sided derivatives. Bounded F families have uniform integrability, without presupposing an exact equation unless the separate positive-lower-mass corollary applies.

The full potential current is paired only with smooth positive tests. The internal unbounded trace-density inequality gives a nonnegative error with exact mass 1-b^(1/n)D_p(T), independent of the subsolution. Along smooth maximizing sequences it vanishes in total variation; the tail hypothesis identifies the limiting probability. No product with a singular limiting test or independence of different maximizers is asserted.

A smooth strictly positive maximizing cofactor makes the full current trace absolutely continuous with Ln coefficients. Countably many local positive matrix tests and the determinant variational formula give determinant equality, hence a scalar times the positive smooth metric. In n>=2 the internal smooth-conformal-current lemma forces the scalar and potential to be smooth. Every threshold subsolution then solves the exact equation and differs only by a constant.

groups.scope: Smooth dual sharpness and dimension-one boundary
groups.checked_argument: Lp exponential compactness plus smooth threshold uniqueness gives uniform convergence. In the closed case the conformal equation forces a positive constant, so smooth positive attainment requires smooth positive density. A Gauduchon cutoff construction supplies a nonclosed example with density zero on an open set. groups.scope: Semipositive attainment off an analytic set
groups.checked_argument: Regularized Gauduchon tests give vanishing trace error; off the proper analytic degeneracy set local determinant equality and smooth conformal-current regularity give the exact equation. Both measures charge no analytic-set mass, yielding the global equation. Ordered analytic rigidity gives uniqueness up to constants, without asserting global smoothness.

Holder duality for the determinant-weighted probability and normalized-potential moments bound the constants by b and b exp(C lambda). Common barriers and greatest-subsolution cluster rigidity give L1 convergence. Capacity convergence additionally requires a nontrivial envelope in a smaller background and follows from the self-error criterion; it is not deduced from L1 convergence alone.

groups.scope: Mass invariance and sublinear envelope criteria
groups.checked_argument: Stretched truncation envelopes use the contact-set domination and a full-mass tail to obtain a lower bound for their supremum. Their decreasing limit gives a competitor in every smaller background. A sublinear lower bound admits a convex-chain competitor with exponent between alpha and one, and forces zero Lelong numbers.

The smooth global root and rank>=2 assumption make wedge by gamma injective on one-forms. A smooth left inverse gives dr=alpha-r beta; analytic-set avoidance by short broken paths yields boundedness and a Lipschitz extension. The weak first-order equation makes the extension smooth. A positive closed residual supported on the analytic set consists of divisorial terms, removed by zero Lelong numbers. Moment or entropy hypotheses alone are not asserted to imply these assumptions.

The Hopf surface mass invariance gives b=1 for a chosen smooth perturbation. The quadric double cover has degree two and rank n-1 along ramification; its explicit bounded potential and cofactor test attain the threshold. Rank>=2 requires n>=3 in that example.

The continuous solution has the threshold normalizer. Semipositive-test uniqueness identifies it with the greatest threshold subsolution; uniform precompactness for Lp data identifies every exponential cluster and gives full-family uniform convergence.

The radial flux q tends from zero to one, directly computing extended full mass. The density is L1 but no Lp with p>1; convex sublinear chains give every smaller-background envelope. A hypothetical semipositive maximizer is t A^(n-1); bounded test coefficients and divergent cofactor eigenvalues force t to zero at the pole, contradicting the strong maximum principle on its connected complement. This does not identify the explicit solution with the greatest subsolution.

The radial tail is L^(-1-n(1-alpha)) dL. Entropy converges exactly for n(1-alpha)>1 and the r-th potential moment for alpha r<n(1-alpha); equality cases have logarithmic divergence. These single-density quantities are distinguished from moment bounds for maximizing-test probabilities.

Normalized trace masses turn the exponential moment bound into an O(lambda) total variation trace error. The positive matrix arithmetic-geometric mean deficit bounds the sum of eigenvalue deviations by 2n sqrt(s delta); Cauchy-Schwarz then gives O(sqrt(lambda)) for all current coefficients on compact sets off the analytic degeneracy set. Singular trace is controlled by the same error. No nonlinear product of coefficient measures is used.

Positive Lelong divisors are components of the analytic degeneracy set. A Bott-Chern relation supplies a global integrable potential; sufficiently small coefficient changes preserve positivity and the extended equation off the set. Both measures vanish on the pluripolar set, and threshold uniqueness makes the relation trivial. Other degeneracy divisors need not be independent.

Half the pullback of Fubini-Study by the squaring map is cohomologous to the background. Its explicit smooth potential has total mass one and cofactor maximizer; its root density behaves like the transverse modulus to exponent 2/n, hence is nondifferentiable even for n=2. The bounded density gives uniform exponential convergence, while the closed-case criterion excludes a strictly positive smooth maximizer.

Jensen against one maximizing sequence gives the normalizer bound and a common lower barrier. The separate smaller-background envelope hypothesis gives capacity convergence of each L1 cluster, and damped-measure continuity identifies the exact equation. Entropy supplies moments via the elementary relative-entropy inequality and uniform integrability for selected attainment, without regularity of the limiting current or full-family uniqueness.

Monotone perturbation limits commute with the infimum of affine Gauduchon quotients. The closed nef formula uses a Kahler perturbation. At zero volume, an attaining positive test implies smooth ddc exactness by the zero-degree lemma; the ruled section example excludes this using a nonzero closed positive current.

Nef approximation and integration on the contracted curve locate the boundary. A positive closed nef top intersection gives a positive lower volume and a Kahler current. On the incidence blowup L^2=LQ=1 and Q^2=0. The cutoff perturbation is nonclosed, bounded below by L/2, and has zero chosen mixed correction. groups.scope: Smooth mass attainment and curvature signs
groups.checked_argument: A lower-mass attaining test supplies a minimizing smooth equation and a constant conformal factor; conversely the first variation forces a Gauduchon solution. Oscillating local gradient tests detect the sign of the second-variation form. Local weighted decreasing products make E_u independent of decomposition and a positive weak limit of smooth energies. Distributional Stokes gives the bounded cubic mass identity. For d eta=alpha+i beta, ddc(i eta wedge bareta)=-(alpha^2+beta^2)/(2pi). Base degree forces the split square to be ddc closed. groups.scope: Vanishing lower mass: root volumes and equations
groups.checked_argument: In dimension three the root volume is 3/sqrt(2) times the square root of the cofactor determinant. A fixed-j smooth approximation preserves this bound, while degrees stay bounded. The smooth equation for the root-volume probability yields masses at most P_j^3/R_j^2, tending to zero for every Hermitian background.

Surface lower mass stays positive by a Gauduchon comparison. Products with projective factors transfer zero lower mass to every dimension>=3. Each fixed smooth-density volume stays positive, so degenerating densities cannot have a uniform upper bound; local smooth-density adjoint estimates are kept distinct from the unrestricted critical family.

For the elliptic quotient ddc D=2 alpha beta and the square of alpha+beta+D is closed. Fiber integration gives mass 24pi. The cubic identity gives the exact vertical energy loss and upper mass 24pi; equality occurs precisely for base-pulled potentials, while zero lower mass remains possible. For potentials f(t)+v(base), positivity implies |f prime|<1 and f double-prime>-1 by vertical testing and the two rulings. The descending-interval integration bounds the mean square of f prime strictly below L-4/3. Volume bounds between c epsilon^n and C give orders in [0,n]. Measure comparison, metric squeezing and bounded logarithmic errors give gauge, scale and perturbation independence. A one-factor Poisson equation yields the exact Schur-complement volume and a conformal Gauduchon minimizer. Finite-order zeros yield fractional orders or logarithmic zero order. A dominating composition of blowups provides a positive metric C p-star h minus an effective exceptional curvature. Poincare-Lelong and rank<=n-2 kill its pairing with pulled-back (n-1,n-1) tests. For the incidence blowup, radial slopes give base total mass (x+y)^m-y^m and cumulative smooth reference masses of order s^m downstairs versus s upstairs. groups.scope: Anticanonical horizontal inverse and fixed point
groups.checked_argument: Closed fiber-holomorphic two-forms decompose into positive homogeneous components only. groups.scope: Rank-one cutoff curvature and nine-point cases
groups.checked_argument: A concave cutoff of the flat logarithmic norm yields smooth semipositive rank-at-most-one curvature supported in a tube annulus. Kahler pairing with the nonempty divisor makes its maximal rank one. Restriction sequences on the rational nine-point blowup give a basepoint-free multiple exactly in the torsion case, while a non-torsion normal bundle leaves only the fixed multiple divisor; order one alone does not distinguish them.

A parametric normal-disk inverse preserves the local parallel defining functions and identifies the flat horizontal foliation smoothly, not holomorphically. Finite holonomy is equivalent to holomorphic torsion by constant modulus on the compact divisor and gives a proper connected-fiber map with divisor mD. Infinite holonomy has dense leaves; maximum modulus on a compact circle level then forces holomorphic functions on the punctured tube to be constant.

A compact hole misses a smaller divisor tube, and connectedness gives constant extension by the identity theorem in the non-torsion case. Any strictly plurisubharmonic function would attain an impossible leafwise maximum on a compact level; finite holonomy instead yields compact positive-dimensional fibers. These arguments require n>=2 and the stated flat-neighborhood hypothesis.

groups.scope: Punctured line hulls and affine elliptic quotient
groups.checked_argument: Fiber Laurent coefficients on a negative line bundle eliminate negative powers, extending functions across the zero section. The compact circle hull contains a sequence tending to the removed zero, so it is not compact. The affine quotient has invariant sigma; generic parameter fibers contain a closed punctured line bundle, exceptional parameters a compact elliptic curve. The complement of the projective diagonal is a smooth affine quadric and an affine-line bundle over P1, hence simply connected and Stein.

The additive elliptic cocycle is nonzero by differentiating a hypothetical entire splitting. Degree normalization uses a flat unitary degree-zero factor. The relative cotangent sequence gives a two-dimensional cohomology with ruling and base components. The explicit affine chart and lattice cocycles recover each extension with nonzero ruling component, and scaling its fiber coordinate identifies its torsor with the non-Stein quotient with Stein universal cover. Projectivization conventions and the sign under duality remain explicit.

groups.scope: Symmetric tensor weights and elliptic cohomology
groups.checked_argument: Holomorphy in the opposite ruling chart bounds coefficient degrees and gives finitely many weights. Positive-degree twists contribute kd(s+1), negative-degree twists nothing, and the nonsplit unipotent block has only the Euler invariant. The coefficient exact sequence is surjective after positive twist. Summing gives 1+d r(r+1)(r+2)/6 and tautological volume d. Quotienting by the Euler variable and the square of positive-weight-index ideal produces infinitely many square-zero degree components, proving nonfinite generation.

groups.scope: Extension section algebras and zero ruling component
groups.checked_argument: The nonzero-ruling homogeneous fiber ring is a quadratic rank-one matrix ring; counting admissible monomials proves no extra relations. Surviving weights are zero and negative. Replacing h by h+(K/q0)w reduces the coefficient bundle to the unipotent block plus a trivial variable, giving an algebra isomorphism with the tangent ring adjoined w and dimension r+1+d binomial(r+3,4). The zero-ruling quadric has the same surviving algebra, but its torsor and universal cover contain compact rational curves and are not Stein.

Hahn-Banach separation from the open positive cone gives a positive order-zero ddc-closed current annihilating the potential space. Normalization proves the exact smooth-positivity and nef thresholds, including the singleton dimension-one current. The full current cone is distinguished from the weak closure of smooth Gauduchon tests. Positive nef volume forces every annihilator determinant measure to vanish, but does not generally determine its support.

The later positive representative gives a uniformly positive affine reference path. The normalized scalar equation has factor 2pi; explicit combinations of its time derivative give two-sided determinant bounds. The torsion trace inequality and reciprocal potential correction give uniform ellipticity. Concave parabolic regularity and Schauder continuation extend to every admissible time. Compact current duality computes the exact lifetime and endpoint annihilator without implying local metric convergence.

groups.scope: Actual flow positive-volume endpoint and twist dependence
groups.checked_argument: The radial initial metric has an explicit Ricci background whose endpoint differs from the nonbig positive-volume model by a smooth potential. Closed localized base tests exclude all later pseudoeffective times. Annihilating currents have trace supported on the singular fiber and a rank-one coefficient matrix by positivity, while uniqueness of their probabilities is not asserted. Nonclosed divisorial removal and current Stokes identify prescribed generic-Lelong feasibility with pseudoeffectivity of the residual background, including the threshold endpoint. A positive smooth residual solves its equation with a smooth remainder; threshold rigidity, with a separate dimension-one mass argument, excludes additional singular subsolutions. Ordinary-type normalizers agree by bounded strict domination. The residual volume and individual unconstrained threshold remain distinct.

groups.scope: Finite divisorial families and Hopf threshold
groups.checked_argument: Finite-dimensional elliptic dependence gives smooth residual remainders through zero coefficients. Fixed analytic support has capacity zero, so coefficient convergence gives capacity and L1 convergence, exact total variation of equation measures, and the divisorial vanishing-order formula on every modification. Multiplier ideals can still jump at integers.
